name: Blind Don
description: Blind Don is the strategic two-player variation of Nine-Card Don, a traditional British pub game from the All Fours family. Popular in Lancashire and South Wales, it features a unique two-part deal where players play through the entire deck in two separate phases. The game centers on capturing high-point cards, particularly the Nines and the 'Don' (Five of Trumps). It is a game of perfect memory, as the cards played in the first half reveal the exact contents of the opponent's hand in the second half.

content.text: Blind Don is the strategic two-player variation of Nine-Card Don, a traditional British pub game from the All Fours family. Popular in Lancashire and South Wales, it features a unique two-part deal where players play through the entire deck in two separate phases. The game centers on capturing high-point cards, particularly the Nines and the 'Don' (Five of Trumps). It is a game of perfect memory, as the cards played in the first half reveal the exact contents of the opponent's hand in the second half.

Descended from the 17th-century game All Fours via the Irish game Dom Pedro. 'Don' emerged as a distinct British regional variant, with Blind Don being the adaptation for two players to maintain the competitive tension of the partnership version.
Standard 52-card French pack. Ranks: A, K, Q, J, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2.

Deal 13 cards to each player. The remaining 26 cards are set aside face-down for the second half of the game. The first card played (the 'pitch') by the non-dealer sets the trump suit for the entire hand.
